1. (Currently Amended) A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising:
a hardware entropy source including at least one ring oscillator;
one or more logic circuits physically coupled to the hardware entropy source and configured to receive a plurality of independent first entropy values from the hardware entropy source;
one or more logic circuits physically coupled to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values and configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value;
one or more logic circuits physically coupled to receive the second entropy value and configured to seed a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
one or more logic circuits physically coupled to the pseudorandom number generator and configured to generate a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
one or more logic circuits physically coupled to receive the random number and configured to produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

2. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code are further configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

3. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code are further configured to at least:
implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

4. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware entropy source is a ring oscillator.

5. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware entropy source is a single ring oscillator.

6. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware entropy source comprises a plurality of independent ring oscillators.

7. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a permutation function.

8. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 7, wherein the one or more logic circuits configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function are further configured to:
divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

9. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a hash function.

10. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a bit-mixer.

11. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function are further configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

12. (Cancelled)

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least:

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware entropy source is a ring oscillator.

21. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a hash function.
